persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Kevin, 58, the volunteer who organizes events at your church in Indiana. On Saturday 14 November 2026 the youth group is holding a flag football tournament, and last year only a few teams came because people heard about it too late. Today you want to plan all the messages to parents and players in good time, so nobody misses it.

challenge.intro: Now you are Kevin. The app is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. Do NOT send any message, and you do not need an AI. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Message Assistant with the normal app link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If it does not show, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK (if it says there is nothing to erase, just tap OK). The boxes in '1 · Tell it once' are empty and 'Your groups' says 'No groups yet'.

tasks.text: Tell the app what you are promoting: the Youth Football Tournament, on Saturday 14 November 2026.
tasks.hint: Section '1 · Tell it once': the first box is what you are promoting, the second box is the big day. Tap the date box and choose 14 November 2026.

tasks.text: Two groups must hear about it: parents and players. You want them to come and register a team.
tasks.hint: In section 1, type the two groups in the 'Who needs to hear about it?' box with a comma between them. The next box asks what you want them to DO.

tasks.text: Tell the app what makes it special: entry is free and the winning team gets a trophy.
tasks.hint: The last box in section 1 is 'Anything else that matters?'.

tasks.text: Make a group called parents with three phone numbers: 847-555-0101, 847-555-0102 and 847-555-0103 (made-up numbers).
tasks.hint: In the card '👥 Your groups', tap '＋ Add a group'. The name must be exactly the same word you used in section 1: parents. Then put all three numbers in, with commas between them (keep the dashes, no spaces inside a number).

tasks.text: You have no AI today. Open the finished example plan, and show that you have already sent its invitation TEXT message (the text, not the email). Do not really send anything.

tasks.hint: Tap '👀 Show me a finished example first'. Find the piece called 'The invitation text' (it says 💬 TEXT) and tap its 'mark sent ✓' button. Not the invitation email.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: plans a series of messages before an event so people do not miss it
writes each message for each group, with an AI helping
you send them yourself and tick each one off; it never sends by itself

lines: Welcome. This short video explains Message Assistant. In about four minutes you will know what it is for and how to use it.
First, the problem. Your group has something coming up. A fundraiser, a rummage sale, a new service time, a grand opening.
You send one message a week before. Many people miss it. Others forget. On the day, only a few come.
Big organizations send a plan of messages instead: a save the date, a reminder, a phone call, a poster, a nudge the day before, a thank you after. That is a campaign.
Message Assistant helps a small group do the same, without a marketing team and without a monthly bill.
Who is it for? Church volunteers, school clubs, small business owners, nonprofits. Anyone who needs people to show up.
One important thing first. Message Assistant never sends anything by itself. It plans and it writes. You decide when to press send, from your own phone.
Let us look at the screen. Section one is called Tell it once. Here you answer five questions.
What are you promoting? For example, Fall Kickoff Party.
The big day, or deadline. Tap the box and choose the date.
Who needs to hear about it? Type your groups, with commas between them. For example, members, neighborhood families.
What do you want them to do? Show up Saturday, come to the sale, give online.
And Anything else that matters is for details and tone, like free food, family-friendly, warm and fun, not salesy.
Your answers are kept on this phone, even if you leave and come back.
The next card is Your groups. It is optional. Tap Add a group, type a name like members, then paste their emails or phone numbers once.
Then any email aimed at that group goes to all of them in one tap, from your own email. Use the same group names you typed in section one, so they match.
Section two is called Let your AI build the campaign. Tap Copy the campaign prompt. It writes the question for you.
Open Claude or ChatGPT, whichever you use, paste, and send. The A.I. writes the whole campaign. Copy its answer, paste it in this box, and tap Build my plan.
No A.I. yet? Tap Show me a finished example first, and you can see a real plan before you make your own.
Your plan appears in section three, one day at a time. Each piece shows its type: email, text, calls, artwork, or social. It shows who it is for, and the full message, ready to use.

Under each piece are buttons. Copy copies the words. A text has Open in Messages, and an email has Open in email. These only open your own app with the words ready. Nothing goes until you press send there.
When you have sent a piece, tap mark sent. For a call or a poster, it says mark done. The piece changes, so you always know what is finished.
At the top of the plan, Put every piece on my calendar saves a file that makes your phone remind you when each piece is due. Print the plan gives you a paper copy.
How to start, in your first two minutes. Fill in the five questions for one real event. Then tap Show me a finished example first, so you know what you are about to get.
When you are ready, copy the prompt into your A.I., paste the answer back, and put the pieces on your calendar.
Everything stays on this phone. There are no accounts and no mailing service to sign up for.
Message Assistant is nineteen dollars, one time.
And the question mark button in the corner has the tour and help any time you need them.

daily.task: Write one new message in Message Assistant (keep it as a draft — don’t send it to anyone).

explore.name: 👀 The finished example
explore.find: Tap 👀 See a finished example first.
explore.try: Look at the whole example plan. Scroll to the end.

explore.name: 1️⃣ Tell it once
explore.try: Fill all five questions. Pick the date. Try an empty “What”, and a very long answer.

explore.name: 👥 Your groups
explore.try: Add a group with two made-up emails. Edit it. Empty the box to remove it.

explore.name: 2️⃣ Let your AI build it
explore.try: Tap 📋 Copy the campaign prompt. Look at open Claude / ChatGPT. Paste some nonsense and tap Build my plan — what does it say?

explore.name: 3️⃣ Your plan
explore.find: Section 3, after a plan is built.
explore.try: Tap 📅 calendar and 🖨 Print (you can cancel). ↻ New campaign asks first — tap no.

explore.name: 🧩 The pieces
explore.try: Tap 📋 Copy on one. Look at the email, Messages and Canva buttons — don’t send. Tap mark sent ✓, then tap it again.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open every line in it: Aa (size), ✨ Ask an AI, 🌉 More from Daraja, 🎬 Take the tour again. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
